title: Traceability audit — the evidence behind declining MLflow
question: does the artifact + superseded/ pattern already provide per-run traceability with preserved predecessors?

T2_reports_record_seed_and_versions.requirement: T2 — every report records seed and package versions

exempt.reason: a text scan of source files; no seed, no numeric result
an inventory of string occurrences; same

T3_predecessors_preserved.requirement: T3 — superseding an artifact preserves its predecessor
T3_predecessors_preserved.enforcement: src/monitoring/artifact_io.py raises ArtifactOverwriteError on an unflagged overwrite and copies the prior version into superseded/auto/ when overwrite is explicit; both behaviours are unit-tested in tests/test_artifact_integrity.py

T4_model_lineage.requirement: T4 — model lineage: data, trigger, promotion evidence

T5_model_binary_provenance.requirement: T5 — model binaries carry provenance and fail on skew
T5_model_binary_provenance.diagnosis: the sidecar machinery exists and is tested, but nothing calls it: models are still written by a bare pickle.dump in trainer.py, so no shipped model records the versions it was fitted under

T6_runs_are_byte_reproducible.requirement: T6 — a re-run is byte-comparable to the original

answer: SUBSTANTIALLY YES, WITH TWO NAMED GAPS
honesty_note: This audit is reported with its failures because an all-green traceability audit written by the same person who built the traceability is not evidence. The gaps below are the useful part.
